newsitem.title: UK: Welsh firm wins Chinese tanker conversion contract.
newsitem.headline: Welsh firm wins Chinese tanker conversion contract.

text.p: A Welsh ship repair company today said it had won the first ever sub-contract from China for work involving the conversion of an oil tanker into a floating production platform.
Harris Pye Marine Ltd said it had won a multi-million stg order from Hyundai's shipyard at Shanhaiguan for the refurbishment of a VLCC for Braziian oil group Petroleo Brasileiro SA - Petrobras.
"It represents a major breakthrough in the Far East market place," said Harris Pye Marine owners Tony Jones and Mike Dawson, "and a big boost to the local economy."

"We have targeted the country for some time and this marketing initiative has borne fruit with this contract, the first of many we believe will be coming out of the People's Republic in the near future," they said in a statement.

The Barry Docks-based company said: "We will send a team of more than 100 local workers to China for four months to equip the tanker for its new seabound role extracting further oil reserves from existing fields."
Work will mainly involve refurbishment of gas turbines, boilers and electricity generating plant on the ship, said administration manager Mark Prendergast.
He said Harris Pye Marine had won the sub-contract in competition with three other preferred sub-contractors nominated by Petrobras.

Prendergast added that the project manager would be going to China next wednesday and that other workers would follow within the next two weeks after the ship had docked and visas had been acquired. -- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + Tel 44 171 542 4087
